title: Create and Configure a GitHub repository
content:
Repositories are created using a GitHub workflow maintained by the DevSecOps team. You can reach out to them here: Inter IKEA GitHub support, in case of questions.

Below is a guide as to what should be written in the various fields when filing the issue request for the workflow to start:

  • Repository Name/s: The name of the repository/repositories without prefix. For example, devops-unused-1

  • Product Area Name: ipex

  • Core Business Name: Range

  • GitHub Parent Team Name/s: ipex-devops

  • Repository Visibility: private(unless otherwise agreed upon)

  • Organization name: Inter-IKEA

The request will be filed immediately whereby a GitHub workflow starts. You can monitor the progress by looking at actions.

It’s up to you whether you want to create one or several repositories. It could be a good idea to create e.g. 3 or 5 new repositories each time this activity is done. This makes it a bit faster to hand out the repositories to other teams; and in the event of a workflow failure, there are already pre-allocated repositories.

In case of internal GitHub issues or problems with the workflow, repositories can still be ordered through Service Now Order a GitHub Repository in Service Now.

How other teams order new repositories: The Slack workflow request

Steps

  1. A new repository is requested in the #devops Slack channel using the workflow, as described in:
    Request a GitHub Repository

  2. A new repository is configured by several scripts that should be executed in a specific order. To simplify our lives, a workflow is available in tools and samples repository automatically applying GitHub Repository Security Rules:

    -> LINK TO WORKFLOW <-

    At the moment, a repository must exist in the organization with the name ipex-devops-unused-<number>.

  3. The repository should be handed over to the team by answering the same Slack conversation.

Repository collaborators and teams

Permission settings are to be applied following the structure:

  • The IPEX team should always have at least Read access. This will ensure we create visibility across teams' codebase to support innersource methodology.

note

ghas-security-team Admins is managed by the organization and we don’t need to bother about it.

New product teams

  • IPEX-DevOps Admins → Admin role (inter-ikea/ipex-devops-admins)

  • <Product team> Admins → Admin role (i.e. Tira, inter-ikea/tira-admins)

  • <Product team> Contributors → Write role (i.e. Tira, inter-ikea/tira-contributors)

  • <Product team> Readers → Read role (i.e. Tira, inter-ikea/tira-readers)

  • IPEX team → Read role (inter-ikea/ipex)
